## Architecture

**Rust decides, AVFoundation and Metal do** (spec §7). The core holds the
project (JSON, spec §5.2), every edit, the composition plan, the per-frame
recipe, the index of a WebM/Matroska file being imported and the WebM file an
`av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm` export writes (its container only; the packets come from Swift). Swift owns windows, gestures, undo, AVFoundation playback and export,
the Metal compositor, media import and its caches and on-device analysis of
the media (Vision and Sound Analysis on the analysis lane, cached per media
in `cache/analysis/`; the core reads only what a tool or op hands it), and
agent dispatch. No
pixel or sample work in Rust; no ffmpeg dependency in the product. The AV1 and
VP9 encoders (SVT-AV1, libvpx; `designs/adr/codec-export.md`) are
platform-side like AVFoundation: Swift calls them through the bridging header,
no `rc_*` export wraps them (spec §11 CX-4).

### FFI contract

- `core/include/framejob_core.h` is a **hand-maintained** C header, the single
  contract between the worlds. **The FFI is three files in lockstep**: a Rust
  `#[no_mangle]` export, its entry in the header, and its wrapper in
  `app/Sources/ReelCore.swift` and its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, **the
  only files that call `rc_*`** (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in
  the file of its area.
- A handle is an immutable project. **Every edit is pure and answers one of
  three arms** (`core/src/outcome.rs`, spec §5.5): applied with the new
  project, an identity, or refused in the rule's own sentence. Only the first
  is an undo step. `ProjectDocument` is the single mutation point and undo is
  its stack of handles.
- Edits are JSON ops through `rc_project_apply`. **The op table is two
  halves**: what an op MEANS is the module doc of `core/src/edit.rs`, and
  what it TAKES — every argument's name, kind and required-ness — is
  `core/src/op_table.rs`, as data, published as JSON Schema by
  `rc_op_schemas`. `ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders,
  `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s tools and spec §6 mirror them — change one, change
  all four — **except that every op TOOL prints the arguments half instead of
  restating it** (`AgentCatalog.opTool`), so an argument added to an op costs
  a sentence of prose there and no schema. A tool that takes more or less
  than its op does says so in `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`, one row and
  one reason each. The envelope's `scope` key addresses an edit inside a
  nest.
- Persisted-state changes bump `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `core/src/format.rs`
  **and** the header.
- Errors: `rc_project_apply` returns NULL three distinguishable ways, and the
  two message channels are never both written. NULL with NEITHER written is
  an identity; NULL with `reason_out` set is a refusal and that string is the
  rule's own sentence; NULL with `err_out` set is invalid input. The first two
  make no undo step and only the third is an error. `"internal error: …"` is a
  caught panic.

### Where a feature lands — the standard recipe

Every shipped feature follows the same shape; putting a step's code anywhere
else is what bloats files:

1. **Core:** the op's semantics in an `impl Project` block in the module of
   its own concern (a new concern is a new module); the row in `edit.rs`'s
   enum and module-doc table, and its arguments in `op_table.rs` (which is
   where `OP_NAMES` comes from); a persisted field with a serde default and a
   `schema_vN.rs`; a new `core/tests/*.rs`. A field lands in the same phase as
   the thing that renders it.
2. **FFI**, only when a new `rc_*` export is needed: Rust → header →
   the ReelCore file of its area.
3. **Swift:** the typed builder in `ReelOps.swift`; a small value or model
   file; an `EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift` with its validator arm; an
   inspector section REGISTERED in `ClipPane.makeSections()`; a menu item in
   `AppDelegate+Menus.swift`; a gesture as a session struct.
4. **MCP mirror:** a handler in `AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`, a catalog entry
   declaring `scope`, and a comment naming the UI path it mirrors.
5. **Documents:** spec §5.2 / §6 / §7.10 for anything they mirror; the map
   entry in the per-side `CLAUDE.md` if a file's role changed; the feature's
   page in `docs/guide/` (and its README highlight and
   `menus-and-shortcuts.md` row when it adds one); the phase's record in its
   road map.
6. **Verify:** as "Verification" below says; then read the change back
   adversarially before committing.

## Rules

- Conventions are Rasterize's — `~/devel/rasterize`'s three `CLAUDE.md`
  files are the parent text for anything not settled here.
- **Every user-visible edit gets an MCP mirror** (spec §7.9): a handler, a
  catalog entry, and a comment naming the UI path. The startup parity check
  in `AgentServer.prepareCatalog()` has SIX parts: catalog names against handler
  names, every op in the core's table against the tools (through
  `rc_op_names`, with an explicit allow-list for ops that deliberately have
  none), each tool's schema shape, that every op tool declares `scope`,
  that every op tool declares the CORE's own arguments for its op — each one
  described, and no description for an argument no op has
  (`AgentServer+Parity.swift`), and that every tool `ModelKeys.keyed` names
  exists and its description carries its key's clause
  (`AgentServer+Parity.swift`, spec §11 CJ-13). What it cannot see is a CALL, which two
  things guard at dispatch: the argument GATE in `AgentServer+Gate.swift`
  compares the caller's keys to the schema the tool published and refuses a
  stranger by name, for all one hundred and twenty-five product tools (and the dev tools,
  road map 11), before any handler runs;
  and the throwing helpers in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` refuse a value a
  handler cannot read by name rather than dropping it.
- **A feature that needs a language or cloud model tests its key through
  `ModelKeys`** (spec §11 CJ-3): presence, the sentence, the control's or
  menu item's mark, the tool's refusal where it would send, and a row in
  `ModelKeys.keyed`.
- **A file at the ~600-line cap gives something up before it takes anything
  on**, as a pure move landed and gated alone; new files are capped at 400
  lines. Frozen files take wiring only. `core/src/edit.rs` and
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift` are exempt (tables, one row per op), and proof
  instruments in `tools/proof/` are held to neither cap. The ledger is
  `wc -l app/Sources/*.swift core/src/*.rs graphic/src/*.rs | sort -rn`; the
  seam a record already named for a file is under "Named next cuts" in
  `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` / `core-file-history.md`.
- **Size rules are per FILE, never per feature.** A brief, design, road map,
  spec or proof never sets a budget on how many lines a feature may add,
  never measures a feature's total against one, and never names code size as
  a reason to cut, trim or drop a feature: a feature takes as much code as it
  needs. Keeping files small is the cap above and its pure moves, nothing
  else (owner, 2026-10-10).
- **A decision in spec §11 is not re-litigated** (`designs/spec/11-decisions/`). A phase that needs a new
  one records it there before the code, not after.
- **`.secrets/` (gitignored) holds the owner's own keys for proofs**, e.g.
  `.secrets/anthropic-key`, read ONLY by `anthropic_key()` in
  `tools/proof/assistant_prompt_eval.py`. Never open, print, grep, copy or
  list its contents; never move a key from it into an argument, the
  environment of a build, a log or a file. A run that spends money still
  needs its explicit flags (`--live --cap <dollars>`); the file's presence
  spends nothing. Every paid proof request is also held to the month's
  budget (spec §11 P-3, P-6) in
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl`; an agent
  never edits it, raises a budget, or points a verification at it.
- **A check only a person at the machine can make is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`**, added in the change that creates it — never a
  `ready-for-human` issue, and never an instrument built to stand in for the
  person (how a pane looks, whether audio plays, a real key's conversation).
  Automate what a script can truly measure; list only the residue.
- Commit only when asked. A commit message says what was verified and what
  is owed, and the road map's record says the same.

## Verifying a build

A local Distribution build is only ever checked, never launched: it loads
Sparkle, which library validation refuses in an ad-hoc signed hardened app
(spec §11 PUB-7). Debug and Release link with `-dead_strip_dylibs`, so they
never load it.

The app is verified by driving the built binary over MCP and comparing what
it renders — not by reading code. Launch your own instance on your own socket
and only ever kill that one (`pgrep -f "MacOS/Frame Job"` lists them, Debug
and Release alike; the products folder tells them apart; another session may
have one running):

```sh
make app-debug
python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch   # prints folder, socket, log, pid
```

Each later command names the printed folder literally
(`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")`, `python3 tools/proof/phaseN_proof.py
<dir>/agent.sock`, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`), because a shell
variable does not survive from one agent command to the next; stop it by the
pid the launcher prints.

The log line `Frame Job agent socket listening at <dir>/agent.sock` says it is
up (`not bound: <reason>` says why not). Drive it with `tools/proof/mcp.py`'s
`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")` (streamable HTTP over the Unix socket), or with
the bundled stdio helper `framejob-mcp` with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set to the same
path: one tool per §6 op, each taking the `scope`
envelope key, plus the app-state tools — `open_project`, `new_project`,
`new_project_from_range`, `save_project`, `close_project`, `get_project`, `import_media`,
`import_captions`, `export_captions`, `transcribe`, `consolidate_media`, `detect_silence`,
`detect_fillers`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `get_transcript`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `split_at_shots`, `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection`, `set_scope`,
`undo`, `redo`, `render_frame`, `export`, `export_status`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `cancel_export`,
`record_screen`, `write_graphic`,
`get_graphic`, `graphic_reference`, `render_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`,
`import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `rename_graphic`,
`restore_graphic`, `list_graphics`, `insert_graphic`, `export_graphic` and `import_graphic`. A Debug or Release build also has the dev tools
(`snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`;
"Seeing the chrome" below; `play_preview`, which plays a window's preview
for a while and answers the frames composed (#127, spec §11 G-36);
`graphic_memory`, which answers the graphic rasters' memory budget, what is
held and kept, and simulates memory pressure (G-37); `loudness_meter`, which
answers a window's live loudness meter (momentary, short-term, integrated,
true peak, the frames measured and its resets) and resets it (road map
"audio" AP7, AU-77); `land_recording`, which lands fixture files as a
finished recording through the recorder panel's door or `record_screen`'s,
so a proof can watch Enhance the microphone when it lands without a
microphone grant (spec §11 AU-69); and
`analysis_job`, which wants a media's analysis under a document's stand-in
owner and returns at once, or waits for every such job and answers their
runs (spec §11 CJ-27); and `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>`, which holds each
analysis job before its first frame, polling cancellation, so a proof can
act during it; and `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, with which a canned analysis
marker is honoured (spec §11 CJ-26); and `transcript_view`, which answers

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.

title: "Set up several cameras"
description: Put each camera on its own track, line them up by their sound, name them, and get a program track ready for a show filmed with more than one camera.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Set up a show filmed with several cameras, such as a podcast with a camera on each guest or an interview with a wide and a close shot, so you can cut between them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio', 'Clip ▸ Split']}
  keys={['⌘T']}
  tools={['sync_audio', 'copy_pieces']}
/>

## How multicam works

There's no special multicam clip. Each camera is an ordinary clip on an ordinary track, and the edit you watch is a **program track** in front of them, made of pieces of whichever camera you want at each moment.

<Steps>

1. Put [one camera on each track](#one-camera-per-track) and line them up.
2. [Name the tracks](#name-the-tracks) after their cameras.
3. Build [the program track](#the-program-track), by hand or with [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
4. Fix single shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

</Steps>

## One camera per track

Put each camera's recording on a track of its own, then line the recordings up in time. **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** does this from their sound: select the recordings and choose it. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

If a camera stopped and started again, its pieces can all sit on the one track.

## Name the tracks

Double-click a track's header and type the camera's name. These names are what **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** lists, and what the Switch by Speaker sheet uses for its cameras and microphones.

When two listed tracks share a name, Frame Job adds each one's position counted from the back, for example "Camera (2)" and "Camera (3)".

1	=== set-up
2	---
3	title: "Set up several cameras"
4	description: Put each camera on its own track, line them up by their sound, name them, and get a program track ready for a show filmed with more than one camera.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	Set up a show filmed with several cameras, such as a podcast with a camera on each guest or an interview with a wide and a close shot, so you can cut between them.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu={['Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio', 'Clip ▸ Split']}
14	  keys={['⌘T']}
15	  tools={['sync_audio', 'copy_pieces']}
16	/>
17	
18	## How multicam works
19	
20	There's no special multicam clip. Each camera is an ordinary clip on an ordinary track, and the edit you watch is a **program track** in front of them, made of pieces of whichever camera you want at each moment.
21	
22	<Steps>
23	
24	1. Put [one camera on each track](#one-camera-per-track) and line them up.
25	2. [Name the tracks](#name-the-tracks) after their cameras.
26	3. Build [the program track](#the-program-track), by hand or with [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
27	4. Fix single shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	## One camera per track
32	
33	Put each camera's recording on a track of its own, then line the recordings up in time. **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** does this from their sound: select the recordings and choose it. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
34	
35	If a camera stopped and started again, its pieces can all sit on the one track.
36	
37	## Name the tracks
38	
39	Double-click a track's header and type the camera's name. These names are what **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** lists, and what the Switch by Speaker sheet uses for its cameras and microphones.
40	
41	When two listed tracks share a name, Frame Job adds each one's position counted from the back, for example "Camera (2)" and "Camera (3)".
42	
43	## The program track
44	
45	[Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) can write the whole program track for you, and it adds its own track.
46	
47	To build the program by hand:
48	
49	<Steps>
50	
51	1. Move the playhead to the start of a camera's clip.
52	2. Select the clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, then <kbd>⌘V</kbd>. The copy lands at the playhead, in sync with the camera. A paste aims at the front track, and with a clip already there it makes a new track in front of the others. That track is your program.
53	3. With the copy selected, move the playhead to a cut and choose **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). Repeat for each cut, selecting the piece the cut falls in each time.
54	4. Select a shot and pick another camera from [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/).
55	
56	</Steps>
57	
58	The paste makes the track itself, so you don't need **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>) here. A track you added first is the front track, so the copy lands on it instead.
59	
60	A pasted copy keeps its sound on, so the same sound plays from the program track and the camera's track until you [mute one of them](/audio/mute-and-solo/). The pieces Switch by Speaker writes have their sound off.
61	
62	An agent builds the program with one `copy_pieces` call per camera. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
63	
64	## Shown or hidden
65	
66	The camera tracks stay underneath the program. Leave them shown and the program track, being in front, covers them. Or hide them with the hide switch in the track header, or **Hide Video** in the header's right-click menu. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
67	
68	Either way they still work as cameras: a hidden track's clips are still listed by Switch Angle and still count for Switch by Speaker.
69	
70	## Microphones
71	
72	Switch by Speaker needs to know which recording hears which person. It works this out from what you've selected.
73	
74	| Selected | What counts as a microphone |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| Clips with their sound on and no picture, such as a recorder or a separate microphone file | Every track holding one |
77	| No clips like that | Each camera that plays sound is its own microphone |
78	| A camera's sound split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** | Never chosen for you, but you can pick it in a **Microphone** pop-up |
79	
80	So keep each person's microphone file on a track of its own, beside the cameras, and select it with them. Only the selected clips on a microphone's track are listened to.
81	
82	The sheet's **Microphone** pop-ups list every track holding a selected clip with its sound on, so you can swap in a detached camera sound or a camera's own sound there. An agent can name a detached camera sound as a microphone too.
83	
84	When the selection comes to exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, Switch by Speaker can't tell people apart by ear, so it decides from their faces. That includes the case where only one camera has sound. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
85	
86	## Related
87

89	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
90	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)

113	<Steps>
114	
115	1. [Synchronize the recordings](#synchronize-first) with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
116	
117	2. Select every camera's clips and every microphone's clips. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click each clip to add it, or <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a band across them. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
118	
119	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it sits right after Synchronize Audio in the **Clip** menu.
120	
121	4. Check the [speaker rows](#speaker-rows) and adjust the [settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) if you need to. The [summary](#the-summary) at the foot of the sheet updates as you do.
122	
123	5. Choose **Switch** or press Return. **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> leaves everything as it was.
124	
125	</Steps>
126	
127	<Shot
128	  name="15h-switch-by-speaker-sheet.sheet"
129	  alt="The Switch by Speaker sheet. Two speaker rows pair the Camera microphone with the Camera track and the Screen microphone with the Screen track. Below them are Wide set to None, Minimum shot 2 s, Cut 0.2 s before speech, Crosstalk shows Wide, Ignore bleed 15 dB, two unticked boxes, and the summary 1 shot: 1 on Camera. Adds 1 clip."
130	/>
131	
132	Afterwards, [fix single shots](#fix-the-result) by hand. Switch by Speaker works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too, on the nest's own tracks.
133	
134	## Synchronize first
135	
136	Switch by Speaker trusts where the clips sit. It doesn't check that they're in sync, so run [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) before it.
137	
138	A camera [slipped](/editing/slip-and-roll/) or dragged afterwards puts its shots out of step with the voices.
139	
140	## When it is offered
141	
142	**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** is available when:
143	
144	- the selection holds clips with a picture on two or more tracks, each of which is a camera
145	- at least one selected clip has its sound on, from a file that has sound
146	- no sheet is open on the window
147	
148	Sound you've split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** never makes its track a camera. The sheet handles up to nine cameras. The command is still offered with more, but the summary then says so and **Switch** stays dimmed.
149	
150	## Speaker rows
151	
152	Each person gets a row, reading **Speaker 1:**, then a microphone pop-up, the word "on", and the camera that shows them. A camera that is its own microphone stays paired with itself, and the rest are paired front to back to start with. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones) for how the microphones are chosen.
153	
154	Each person needs their own microphone and a camera. A pop-up offers **None** only where the selection left that row with nothing to pair. Leave it on **None** and the summary says what's missing.
155	
156	Change the rows when the front-to-back guess puts someone on the wrong camera. The microphones listed come from your selection, and the cameras from the tracks holding your selected pictures.
157	
158	With exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, the rows are replaced by a different layout. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
159	
160	## The range
161	
162	The cut covers the [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when one is set, otherwise the whole length of the selected camera clips.
163	
164	Only the selected clips of a microphone's track are listened to. A camera track offers all its clips with a picture, selected or not, so an unselected clip on a camera track can still supply shots.
165	
166	## The summary
167	
168	The line under the controls says what **Switch** will do, for example "22 shots: 8 on Cam A, 14 on Cam B. Adds 23 clips." Cameras appear in the order they first show.
169	
170	When Switch can't go ahead, every reason replaces that line, one per line, and **Switch** stays dimmed. The sheet works this out again at every change, so change any control to check again.
171	
172	| The summary says | What it means |
173	| --- | --- |
174	| "The microphone on track … is still being analysed…" | Frame Job hasn't finished measuring that file's loudness or detecting its speech, which can happen straight after an import. Give it a moment, then change any control to check again. |
175	| "The microphone on track … has no speech between … and …, so it never says who is talking." | That microphone hears no speech in the range. Check you've paired the right track, or shorten the range. |
176	| "No angle has a picture between … and …." | No camera covers that stretch of the range. Set an In–Out range that avoids it, or fill the gap. |
177	| "The speaker on track … has no microphone." | A row has no microphone that's selected and sounding. |
178	| "The microphone on track … has no angle to show its speaker." | A row has no camera. |
179	| "Track … is the microphone for 2 speakers; each person needs their own microphone." | One microphone is on two rows. See [Good to know](#good-to-know) for when that's allowed. |
180	| "Switch by Speaker takes at most nine angles…" | More than nine tracks hold a selected picture. Select fewer. |
181	| "Switch by Speaker would add … clips to …; the most is 4096 — raise the minimum shot." | A project holds at most 4,096 clips. Raise [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) for fewer, longer shots. |
182	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Switch by Speaker cannot tell who is talking." | The on-device speech model can't run here, so the command can't work. |
183	| "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job couldn't read the project's sound just then. |
184	
185	An "angle" in these lines is a camera. The track number is Frame Job's own number for the track, not its position on the timeline. With one shared microphone, [two more lines](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode) can appear.
186	
187	**Switch** checks everything once more when you press it. If it can't go ahead at that moment, the reason shows in the summary and the sheet stays open.
188	
189	## How it chooses the shots
190	
191	- A cut lands a moment before each new speaker's first word. [**Cut**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-before-speech) sets how long.
192	- Silence holds the current shot, and so does a reply under a second long.
193	- A pause under half a second between one person's words doesn't end their turn.
194	- The cut opens on the [Wide](/multicam/switch-settings/#wide), the camera you've chosen for your wide shot, when there is one, otherwise on the first speaker's camera. With no Wide and nobody taking a turn, the range is one shot on the front-most camera.
195	- When two people talk at once, [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
196	- Where a shot's camera has nothing to show, that stretch goes to the Wide, else the camera before it, else the front-most camera that covers it.
197	- A shot under [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) merges into a neighbour.
198	
199	## Linked cameras
200	
201	A camera clip still linked to its detached sound can't be switched. The sheet says so and names the clip, ending "Attach Audio first". Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to put the two back together, then try again.
202	
203	Only a linked camera clip crossing the range stops the cut.
204	
205	## One undo step
206	
207	**Switch** writes all of this as one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**. The selection stays. A selected clip cut at the range's ends brings its new half into the selection.
208	
209	### The Program track
210	
211	Switch adds a track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera. It holds a piece of the chosen camera for each shot, in sync, with the picture on and the sound off.
212	
213	To write over an earlier Program track instead, use [**Write to**](/multicam/switch-settings/#write-to).
214	
215	### Cameras hidden
216	
217	Switch hides the camera tracks so only the program shows.
218	
219	A camera track that holds anything outside the range, or any clip without a picture, isn't hidden. Its clips are cut at the range's ends and their pictures are switched off inside the range only.
220	
221	### What stays untouched
222	
223	Nothing outside the range changes. The microphones aren't edited, so what you hear stays the same, apart from any camera sound you chose to [mute](/multicam/switch-settings/#mute-the-cameras-own-sound).
224	
225	## Fix the result
226	
227	- To show a different camera for one shot, select the shot and use [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
228	- To move a cut, [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) it.
229	- To try other settings, choose **Switch by Speaker…** again while the clips are still selected, and pick the old track under **Write to**. Or undo and start over.
230	
231	## Good to know
232	
233	- One microphone on two rows stops the cut when other rows have their own microphones. If you point every row at one microphone, Frame Job reads faces instead, and the summary starts with its [warning](/multicam/one-microphone/#faces-only-guess).
234	- Switch by Speaker doesn't remember your pairing. The speaker rows open fresh each time.
235	
236	## With an agent
237	
238	[`switch_by_speaker`](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch_by_speaker) takes the sheet's values and a few it doesn't show. An agent can name the range directly, which takes priority over the In–Out range, and pair people by hand. It can also ask for the shots without editing anything, and set the shortest turn that cuts and how far one microphone must lead to count alone. See [Switch by Speaker from an agent](/multicam/copy-pieces/#switch-by-speaker-from-an-agent).
239

248	---
249	title: "Switch by Speaker settings"
250	description: What each row of the Switch by Speaker sheet does, its default and range, and which values Frame Job remembers.
251	---
252	
253	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
254	
255	These rows of the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet shape the cut: where it opens, how long shots last, and how it treats two people talking at once.
256	
257	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…" tools="switch_by_speaker" />
258	
259	| Row | What it does | Default | Range |
260	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
261	| [**Wide:**](#wide) | Your wide shot, which opens the cut and shows during crosstalk | The one camera no person uses, otherwise None | Any camera, or None |
262	| [**Minimum shot:**](#minimum-shot) | The shortest shot allowed | 2 s (3 s with [one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)) | 0.5 to 30 s |
263	| [**Cut:**](#cut-before-speech) | How long before speech the cut comes | 0.2 s | 0 to 1 s |
264	| [**Crosstalk:**](#crosstalk-shows) | What shows while two people talk at once | Wide | Wide, Current speaker |
265	| [**Ignore bleed:**](#ignore-bleed) | How far below a speaker's level a voice is ignored | 15 dB | 3 to 40 dB |
266	| [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after) | Breaks up a long monologue | Off | 2 to 600 s |
267	| [**Mute the cameras' own sound**](#mute-the-cameras-own-sound) | Turns the cameras' sound off inside the range | On when no microphone is on a camera track | |
268	| [**Write to:**](#write-to) | Where the cut goes | A new Program track | |
269	
270	The number fields take up to two decimal places.
271	
272	## Wide
273	
274	The camera for your wide shot. Choose any of the cameras, or **None**. If exactly one camera is left over once every person has theirs, it's picked to start with. Otherwise the row opens on **None**.
275	
276	The Wide shows:
277	
278	- at the start of the cut
279	- during crosstalk, when [**Crosstalk**](#crosstalk-shows) shows **Wide**
280	- after [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after)
281	- for a stretch where another camera has nothing to show
282	
283	When nobody is talking, the current shot holds. It doesn't go to the Wide.
284	
285	## Minimum shot
286	
287	The shortest shot the cut may have, from 0.5 to 30 s. The default is 2 s.
288	
289	A shorter shot merges into the shot before it when that camera covers the stretch, otherwise into the shot after it. A short shot that neither neighbour covers stays.
290	
291	Raising this is also the way out when the cut would add more clips than a project can hold.
292	
293	## Cut before speech
294	
295	The **Cut:** row sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes, from 0 to 1 s. The default is 0.2 s, and the cut lands on a whole frame.
296	
297	## Late cuts under heavy bleed
298	
299	A cut is timed from where a voice first rises above its [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line and the microphone's quiet background, not from the word itself. So with heavy bleed in a noisy room, a cut can land later than **Cut** asks. In the worst case measured, with another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the cut came about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.
300	
301	## Crosstalk shows
302	
303	What the program shows while two people talk at once for a second or more. **Wide** cuts to the [Wide](#wide), and **Current speaker** holds the shot you're on. With no Wide chosen, crosstalk holds the current shot whatever this says.
304	
305	Crosstalk shorter than a second starts nothing. A stretch under half a second between two bursts of crosstalk counts as crosstalk.
306	
307	Two microphones are crosstalk when both hear a voice above their [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line. If one leads the other by 8 dB or more, measured against each one's own speaker, it counts alone.
308	
309	## Ignore bleed
310	
311	Every microphone also hears the other people, quieter. A voice more than this far below a microphone's own speaker is bleed, and never counts as that person talking. It runs from 3 to 40 dB, and the default is 15 dB.
312	
313	- Raise it if a quiet guest is never shown.
314	- Lower it if someone is shown while only the other person talks.
315	
316	A voice must also stand 6 dB above the microphone's quiet background to count. This row doesn't appear in the [one-microphone sheet](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode).
317	
318	## Cut to the wide after
319	
320	Breaks up a long monologue. Tick the box and set how long one person may hold the screen, from 2 to 600 s. It's off by default, and the field offers 20 s.
321	
322	When a shot reaches that length, the Wide shows for one [**Minimum shot**](#minimum-shot), then the speaker's camera returns. This repeats to the end of the shot.
323	
324	It needs a Wide. With **Wide** on **None**, ticking it does nothing.
325	
326	## Mute the cameras' own sound
327	
328	Switches the cameras' scratch sound, the rough sound each camera recorded for itself, off inside the range. It's ticked to start with when no microphone is on a camera track, which is when the microphones are separate recordings.
329	
330	It never touches a microphone's track, so a camera used as a microphone keeps its sound.
331	
332	## Write to
333	
334	Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another. Choose **Replace the shots on** and the track's name, or leave it on **A new Program track**, the default.
335	
336	The row shows only when an earlier track can be replaced. That track must:
337	
338	- be unlocked
339	- hold no selected clip
340	- sit in front of the cameras
341	- have something in the range
342	- hold only pieces of the cameras there
343	
344	The track is cleared over the range and cut at its ends. Nothing on it outside the range changes.
345	
346	## Remembered values
347	
348	**Minimum shot**, **Cut**, **Crosstalk** and **Ignore bleed** are kept for the next time. They're written only when you change a value and press **Switch**, so **Cancel** keeps the old ones.
349	
350	**Minimum shot** isn't remembered in the one-microphone sheet. Every other row opens fresh each time. An agent's call reads none of the remembered values and uses the defaults in the table above.
351	
352	## With an agent
353	
354	`switch_by_speaker` takes these rows as `wide`, `min_shot`, `lead`, `crosstalk`, `bleed_db`, `wide_after`, `mute_cameras` and `track`. See [its options](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch-by-speaker-options).

365	description: When one microphone hears everyone, let Switch by Speaker decide who is talking from the cameras' pictures, and check the result.

367	
368	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
369	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
370	
371	When one microphone hears everyone, it can't say who's talking. [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) then decides from the cameras' pictures instead, by watching whose mouth is moving.
372	
373	<AtAGlance
374	  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
375	  tools="switch_by_speaker"
376	  needs="Nothing. Face detection and speech detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
377	/>
378	
379	## One microphone for everyone
380	
381	Frame Job works this way when your selection holds exactly one microphone and two or more cameras. That includes a selection where only one camera has sound. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones).
382	
383	<Steps>
384	
385	1. Line the recordings up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
386	
387	2. Select the cameras' clips and the microphone's clip, then choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**.
388	
389	3. If the cameras haven't been read yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#finding-faces-first).
390	
391	4. Check [the sheet](#the-sheet-in-this-mode) and choose **Switch**.
392	
393	5. [Look through the result](#faces-only-guess) and fix any wrong shots.
394	
395	</Steps>
396	
397	While the microphone hears speech, the camera whose person's mouth moves most is shown:
398	
399	- Each camera's person is the largest face in its picture.
400	- Frame Job watches that mouth opening and closing over half a second.
401	- A camera wins when its mouth moves at least half as much again as the next camera's (1.5×) and more than a small minimum.
402	- When two mouths move alike, or the busiest mouth stays under that minimum, it's crosstalk, and [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
403	- With no speech, or no mouth to read, the current shot holds.
404	
405	The rest of the cut works as it does with several microphones, and it writes the same [Program track](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/#the-program-track) as one undo step.
406	
407	## Finding faces first
408	
409	Frame Job reads faces from its [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of each camera. When a camera's faces haven't been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet comes up first, with a bar for each file. The Switch by Speaker sheet opens once they're found.
410	
411	Only the part of each camera the range needs is analysed, and what's found is kept in the project's cache, so next time it's quicker or skipped.
412	
413	| If | Then |
414	| --- | --- |
415	| You choose **Stop** | Everything stays as it was, and what was saved so far is kept. Frame Job saves as it goes, every 30 seconds. Choose the command again to carry on. |
416	| The analysis fails | Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
417	| The project changed while it analysed | Frame Job beeps, says so at the foot of the inspector, and switches nothing. Choose the command again. |
418	
419	## The sheet in this mode
420	
421	The sheet changes to suit one microphone:
422	
423	- One **Microphone:** pop-up replaces the speaker rows, and **Cameras:** lists every camera.
424	- There's no **Ignore bleed** row, because there's no second microphone to bleed into.
425	- **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s, not 2 s, and isn't remembered.
426	- **Wide** opens on **None**.
427	
428	The other rows work as they do in [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/).
429	
430	A camera with no face whose mouth can be read stops the cut. The summary reads "The camera on track … shows no face whose mouth can be read between … and …, so it never says who is talking." A camera whose faces still aren't found reads "The camera on track … is still being analysed — its faces have not been found yet. Try again in a moment."
431	
432	## Wide in this mode
433	
434	Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk. That camera then takes no part in deciding who talks, so a true wide shot whose faces are too small to read won't stop the cut. With no Wide, crosstalk holds the current shot.
435	
436	With only two cameras, making one the Wide leaves a single camera for faces to decide between. Faces no longer decide and the warning leaves the summary. The cut then opens on the Wide, moves to the other camera at the first turn of speech, and stays there unless [**Cut to the wide after**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-to-the-wide-after) breaks it up.
437	
438	## Faces only guess
439	
440	The summary starts "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
441	
442	Frame Job measures only how much each mouth moves while the microphone hears speech, so a mouth that moves without speaking, such as laughing or chewing, can put a cut in the wrong place. A face turned away gives no mouth to read, so that camera can't be chosen while it's turned, even if that person is the one talking. Look through the result and fix those shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
443	
444	## Good to know
445	
446	- Only the largest face in a camera is read. With two people in one shot, the other person's mouth doesn't count.
447	- Only video files are read for faces. A still picture on a camera track has no mouth to read.
448	- Pointing every speaker row at one microphone in the ordinary sheet also reads faces. It doesn't bring up the Analyzing sheet, so a camera not yet read stays "still being analysed". To find its faces, change the selection so it comes to [one microphone](/multicam/set-up/#microphones), and choose the command again.
449	
450	## With an agent
451	
452	There's no Analyzing sheet for [`switch_by_speaker`](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch_by_speaker). The call waits up to 60 seconds for the faces, then stops, keeping what was saved so far, and calling it again carries on. Its answer says which way it decided and repeats the warning. See [Waiting for faces](/multicam/copy-pieces/#waiting-for-faces).

463	description: Re-pick one shot of your program from another camera, in sync, over exactly the same span.
464	---
465	
466	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
467	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
468	
469	Switch Angle replaces one shot with another camera's picture over exactly the same span. Use it to fix a single cut after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/), or to pick shots by hand. Your cameras need to be [lined up on tracks of their own](/multicam/set-up/) first.
470	
471	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸" tools="switch_angle" />
472	
473	## Switch to another camera
474	
475	<Steps>
476	
477	1. Select the one shot you want to change, usually a clip on your [program track](/multicam/set-up/#the-program-track).
478	
479	2. Open **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**. The submenu [lists the cameras](#the-camera-list) that cover the whole shot.
480	
481	3. Choose a camera.
482	
483	</Steps>
484	
485	The whole switch is one undo step, called **Switch Angle**. The new clip is selected afterwards, or all of them if the shot became [several pieces](#a-camera-that-stopped-and-started). Switch Angle has no keyboard shortcut.
486	
487	## The camera list
488	
489	The submenu lists, front track first, every other track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. Frame Job writes the list each time the menu opens, so it always matches the current selection.
490	
491	- Only clips of a video file with a picture count. Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests don't.
492	- A clip with its picture switched off still counts, and so does a clip on a hidden track. That's what keeps your cameras in the list after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) has hidden them or turned their pictures off.
493	- The list stops at nine tracks. A tenth covering track, further back, isn't listed.
494	
495	### Tracks with the same name
496	
497	When two listed tracks share a name, each gets its position counted from the back track, for example **Camera (2)** and **Camera (3)**. A name only one listed track has appears as it is.
498	
499	### No Covering Angle
500	
501	The submenu holds a single greyed item, **No Covering Angle**, when there's nothing to switch to. That happens when you haven't selected exactly one clip, or when no track covers the selected clip. This item is never available.
502	
503	### Greyed cameras
504	
505	The cameras are listed but greyed when the switch can't be made:
506	
507	| Why it's greyed | What to do |
508	| --- | --- |
509	| The shot's track is locked. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
510	| The shot is linked to a detached sound. | Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
511	| A sheet is open on the window. | Close the sheet. |
512	
513	## What the switch does
514	
515	The shot is replaced by the camera's picture on the shot's own track, over the same span and in sync. The new clip shows the camera's own frame at every moment, so a cut to it lands exactly where the old shot's cut did.
516	
517	### A camera that stopped and started
518	
519	A shot can cross the end of one of the camera's clips and the start of the next, when the camera stopped and started again. The shot then becomes two pieces, one from each file, meeting at a plain cut. A shot that crosses more of the camera's clips gets one piece for each.
520	
521	### Overlapping camera clips
522	
523	Where two of a camera's clips overlap, as they do across a transition, the later one takes over at its own start. The shot gets a piece of each, meeting at a plain cut, so a transition between those two clips doesn't appear in the shot.
524	
525	## What the shot keeps and loses
526	
527	The shot keeps:
528	
529	- Its span on the timeline.
530	- Whether its picture and its sound are on. A shot with its sound off gives you a new clip with its sound off, whatever the camera's clip has.
531	- The [transitions](/motion/transitions/) at both of its edges, with their kind, curve and audio shape.
532	
533	Nothing else carries over. A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied to the new camera's piece. The piece is cut from the camera's own clip, so it has that clip's settings instead.
534	
535	## A transition that no longer fits
536	
537	A transition needs the two clips to overlap by its length. When the camera's first or last piece is too short for that, Frame Job drops that transition and makes the switch anyway, leaving a plain cut at that edge. The undo step then reads **Switch Angle (transition removed)**, so you can see that it happened.
538	
539	## When a switch fails
540	
541	When a switch can't be done, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message gives clips and tracks by number, and times in ticks, 600,000 to the second.
542	
543	| The message says | What it means |
544	| --- | --- |
545	| "clip 7's edge is held at tick …, short of tick …, so clip 9 cannot be re-picked" | The clip next to the shot plays a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) that can't give up the transition's frames. The message names that clip and the shot. |
546	| "track 3 does not cover clip 12: nothing with a picture plays on it at tick …" | The camera doesn't cover the shot, and the message names the first moment it doesn't. The menu only lists cameras that cover the shot, so this one normally comes back to an agent calling `switch_angle`. |
547	
548	## Good to know
549	
550	- Switch Angle works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own tracks.
551	- Only the shot's track has to be unlocked. A locked camera track is still listed, and you can switch to it.
552	- Frame Job doesn't check what kind of clip you've selected. A text or picture clip with a camera covering it gets replaced in the same way.
553	- A shot that becomes several pieces adds clips. At the project's limit of 4,096 clips, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes, with no message.
554	
555	## With an agent
556	
557	[`switch_angle`](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch_angle) makes the same switch, and it takes the shot and the camera's track directly, so an agent isn't held to the menu's nine tracks. It returns the new clips rather than selecting them. To work inside a nest, open it with `set_scope` first, because the tool doesn't take `scope`.
558	
559	To lay a whole program out at once rather than one shot at a time, an agent can use [`copy_pieces`](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
560	
561	## Related
562	
563	- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
564	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
565	- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
566	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
567	- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
568	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)
569	=== copy-pieces
570	---
571	title: "Copy pieces to another track (agents)"
572	description: How an agent builds a program from synced cameras with copy_pieces, and what it can do with switch_by_speaker that the sheet can't.
573	---
574	
575	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
576	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
577	
578	An [agent](/mcp/overview/) can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. This page is for anyone driving Frame Job from an agent. The exact arguments and results of each tool are in [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
579	
580	<AtAGlance
581	  where="No menu item of its own. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ and Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… write with it."
582	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_by_speaker', 'switch_angle']}
583	  needs="Nothing. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac."
584	/>
585	
586	## Copy pieces of a clip
587	
588	`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.
589	
590	| Argument | What it does | Required |
591	| --- | --- | --- |
592	| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
593	| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
594	| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]`, at least one pair. These are times on the timeline, in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
595	| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
596	| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
597	
598	The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. To work inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), pass `scope`, and the times and tracks are then the nest's own.
599	
600	### What a piece is
601	
602	Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal and a graphic's own timeline, and its actions and timed words are cut the way a split cuts them.
603	
604	A piece gets a new id, has no transition, and isn't linked to any detached sound.
605	
606	### How ranges are read
607	
608	- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
609	- A pair written backwards is the same range.
610	- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
611	- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.
612	
613	## Cut a whole program from the cameras
614	
615	An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.
616	
617	<Steps>
618	
619	1. Add the program track with `add_track`, naming it. With no `index` it goes to the front, in front of the cameras.
620	
621	2. For each camera clip, call `copy_pieces` with that clip, the program track, and every stretch where the camera is on screen. This takes the stretches from 0 to 5 seconds and from 10 to 15 seconds:
622	
623	   ```json
624	   { "clip": 12, "track": 5, "ranges": [[0, 3000000], [6000000, 9000000]], "audio": false }
625	   ```
626	
627	3. If the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` as above so the pieces stay silent, and mute the camera tracks with `set_track`, because they keep playing their own sound behind the program.
628	
629	</Steps>
630	
631	A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips.
632	
633	To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
634	
635	## When a copy won't happen
636	
637	Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:
638	
639	1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
640	2. A range falls outside the clip.
641	3. Two ranges overlap.
642	4. The destination track is locked.
643	5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The error names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.
644	
645	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
646	
647	## Switch by Speaker from an agent
648	
649	`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.
650	
651	- Run `sync_audio` first. It trusts where the clips sit and doesn't check that they're in sync.
652	- Set the clips with `set_selection`, because it reads the selected clips.
653	- Every argument is optional, including who's who (`speakers`), the range (`from` and `to`) and the track to replace (`track`).
654	- The sheet pulls a number back into its range. The tool stops with an error instead, and nothing changes.
655	- To work inside a nest, open it with `set_scope` first, because the tool doesn't take `scope`.
656	
657	### Preview the cut
658	
659	Pass `apply: false` to see the shots without editing anything. The result lists each shot's camera, start and end, how many edits it would make and how many clips it would add, and nothing in the project moves. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
660	
661	The result has `applied: false` and no `step`, and `track` is null unless you named one. Leave `apply` out and the edit is made.
662	
663	### Values only an agent can set
664	
665	| Argument | What it does | Default | Range |
666	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
667	| `min_turn` | The shortest turn that cuts. A shorter turn, such as a quick reply, starts no shot. | 1 s | 0.2 to 10 s |
668	| `dominance_db` | How far one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. Below that lead, two active microphones are crosstalk. | 8 dB | 0 to 30 dB |
669	
670	### Check which mode ran
671	
672	Every result has a `mode`, either `microphones` or `faces`.
673	
674	Faces mode is [cutting from one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/). You get it by naming one microphone for two or more cameras, and it's the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone. In this mode:
675	
676	- The result's `note` reads "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
677	- `min_shot` is 3 s unless you give it.
678	- A camera you name as `wide` takes no part in deciding who's talking.
679	
680	### Waiting for faces
681	
682	Where **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** would show the Analyzing sheet first, the tool waits for the faces, for up to 60 seconds. Past that it stops with nothing switched, and what it found is kept. Call it again to continue.
683	
684	If the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project changes during the wait, nothing is switched either.
685	
686	### When Switch by Speaker won't run
687	
688	If any of these applies, the call stops and nothing changes. Frame Job checks this first group together and names every one that applies, so you can fix them in one go:
689	
690	- Under two cameras, or over nine. A camera here is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
691	- A person without a microphone or without a camera.
692	- One microphone for two people, outside faces mode.
693	- A microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range.
694	- Speech detection isn't available on this Mac.
695	- A camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read.
696	- A stretch no camera covers.
697	
698	These each stop the call on their own:
699	
700	- A faces analysis that failed, was stopped or ran past the wait.
701	- A project that changed during the wait.
702	- More clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
703	- A track named to replace that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera.
704	- A camera clip linked to its detached sound. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.
705	
706	## Related
707	
708	- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
709	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
710	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
711	- [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/)
712	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
713	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)
